title: Department of Agrarian Reform v. Sarangani Agricultural Co.
summary: The Supreme Court clarified the scope of CARP coverage, ruling that the reclassification of agricultural land to non-agricultural use prior to the effectivity of CARL exempts the land from agrarian reform coverage. The date of reclassification is the determinative factor.
doctrine: Lands reclassified from agricultural to non-agricultural use by the local government unit or by the DAR prior to June 15, 1988 are exempt from CARP coverage. The determinative factor is the date of reclassification, not the actual use of the land at the time of coverage.
fullText:
BERSAMIN, J.:

The issue is whether the subject property, which was reclassified from agricultural to non-agricultural use, falls within the coverage of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program.

Section 4 of RA 6657 provides that the CARL shall cover all public and private agricultural lands. However, lands reclassified by proper government authority before the effectivity of the CARL on June 15, 1988 are exempt from CARP coverage.

The Court has consistently held that the reclassification of agricultural land to non-agricultural use before the effectivity of the CARL removes the land from its coverage. What determines whether a land is agricultural is its classification at the time of CARP coverage.
